question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x+y}{3}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{9},\,\text{E}[Y]=\frac{5}{9},\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.5329,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.2833,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\cdot \frac{x+y}{3}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{x{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{x}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}-(\frac{11}{9})(\frac{5}{9}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{81}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{(-\frac{1}{81})}{(0.5329)\cdot (0.2833)} \\  & ≈-0.08,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
